title: A-Flow Artifact Lifecycle Result
description: Result of one artifact review lifecycle. Flow: submission -> runtime identity and prior-state check -> gap_finding -> gap_fixing when required -> unresolved barrier -> evaluation -> at most one bounded evaluation repair cycle -> success_criteria -> fixture_design -> improved artifact. Status is exactly improved | unresolved_gap | skip | error. If any identified gap remains unresolved, evaluation, success_criteria, and fixture_cases are null. The fixture_design stage produces fixture_cases. A failed first evaluation produces structured re-fix findings and receives one additional gap_fixing attempt followed by one final evaluation; evaluation_repair records that cycle's evidence. No artifact change, or a final evaluation that still finds deficiencies, produces unresolved_gap. The final evaluation must verify that the reported deficiencies were corrected while preserving explicit intent, exclusions, scope, and artifact type. An improved result is advisory and non-mutating: no identified gap remains unresolved, evaluation passed, and success criteria plus fixture cases exist. Recorded-removal-v1 is permitted only for gap_finding and gap_fixing output; evaluation, success_criteria, and fixture_design are validated strictly as emitted, and a repaired output must include output_repaired, output_repairs, and repair_policy together. Identity is derived by the runtime. content_digest identifies canonical artifact content; submission_digest also includes artifact_type, intent, and context. An unchanged submission reuses its existing active or completed lifecycle (submission_disposition records replay). A changed submission starts a new lifecycle; artifact_revision advances only when canonical content changes. lifecycle_run_id, started_at, and completed_at identify the run that performed the review. Active-run and invalid-persisted-state outcomes are bounded non-completed error results.

oneOf.description: Completed lifecycle whose evaluation passed: the improved artifact is advisory and execution-ready.

original_artifact.description: The submitted artifact text exactly as received, never canonicalized.

findings.description: Non-blocking observations recorded by a passed evaluation. Deficiencies never appear here: a deficiency forces passed false and the bounded repair cycle instead.

oneOf.description: Completed lifecycle blocked by the unresolved barrier: downstream evaluation output, success_criteria, and fixture_cases are null. When the block came from a failed final evaluation, evaluation_repair.final_evaluation preserves that failure as diagnostic evidence.

original_artifact.description: The submitted artifact text exactly as received, never canonicalized.

oneOf.description: Submission never started a lifecycle (wrong status, empty content, or missing artifact_id).

Bounded active-run response: an identical submission arrived while a prior run for the same submission_digest is still active. Carries the active run's identity; no completed_at because that run has not finished. Reattach with aflow_last_result once it completes.

lifecycle_run_id.description: Identity of the already-active run, not a new one.

oneOf.description: Bounded structured diagnostic: the newest persisted result for this artifact is corrupt or incomplete. Never treated as a completed outcome, never persisted (persisting would bury the damaged file), and carries no run identity because no lifecycle ran. Recovery: inspect or remove the file at state_path, then resubmit.

state_path.description: Filesystem path of the damaged persisted result.

failure.description: corrupt: unreadable or not a result object; incomplete: missing or invalid status.

oneOf.description: A started lifecycle ended in a bounded stage or configuration error. Full runtime-derived identity is present; errors are never replayed, so resubmission retries.
Transport-level error emitted before any lifecycle identity exists: tool input validation, dispatch, missing last result, or an unexpected engine exception.

submission_disposition.description: started: this result came from a lifecycle run this submission triggered (persisted records always say started). replayed: an unchanged resubmission returned the persisted completed result without running any stage.

submission_digest.description: SHA-256 over canonical content plus artifact_type, intent, and context. Unchanged submission_digest reuses the existing completed lifecycle (replay) or reports the active run; changed submission_digest starts a new lifecycle. A new lifecycle does not always imply a new content revision.

content_digest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical artifact content. Canonicalisation is line-ending normalization only (CRLF and CR become LF); all other whitespace is significant, so the digest is safe for patches, source code, YAML, and whitespace-sensitive templates. original_artifact always retains the submitted text verbatim.

artifact_revision.description: Runtime-derived revision sequence for this artifact_id. Advances only when content_digest changes; a new lifecycle with unchanged canonical content keeps its revision.

timestamp.description: Runtime-derived ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. The runtime guarantees completed_at is never earlier than started_at.

repair_policy.description: Unknown-field removal is permitted only for gap_finding and gap_fixing output, bounded by the repair ceiling; evaluation, success_criteria, and fixture_design output is validated strictly as emitted. Present only together with output_repaired and output_repairs.

evaluation_repair_cycles.description: Explicit count of bounded evaluation repair cycles: 0 means none ran; 1 means exactly one ran and evaluation_repair records its evidence. Never more than one.

evaluation_repair.description: Evidence that the single bounded evaluation repair cycle actually occurred: the structured re-fix findings derived from the failed first evaluation, the before/after canonical digest comparison used for no-progress detection, the re-fix gap_fixing output, and the final evaluation (null when it never ran: re-fix hit the unresolved barrier, made no progress, or errored).

after_content_digest.description: Equal to before_content_digest exactly when the cycle made no progress.

refix_finding.description: Structured re-fix contract entry derived in code from one failed-evaluation finding; the model never classifies resolvability.
